contract: WhyFS 1.0 performance contract, part B: spawn stress x300 (BENCHMARK.md)
frozen: 2026-09-28, before the authoritative release-candidate run; derived only from calibration runs of the frozen implementation (product code of ec52053)
frozen_implementation: ec52053 (identical product code in 37f7e7a and later candidates; the only later product change is the diagnostics-only WHYFS_DIAG_NATIVE_ARGS switch in daemon.py)
whyfs_controlled_rule: FAIL only if the lower bound of the CI90 of (median normal pairs - median discard pairs) exceeds the ceiling, i.e. only on evidence that WhyFS's own share of the wall-time overhead is larger than 3.0 percentage points.  Frozen-implementation estimates: Windows x64 +0.71 and +0.79 pp (hosted), -0.64 and +0.23 pp (desktop); Linux x86-64 +1.68 pp; Linux ARM64 +2.67 pp (CI90 +0.63..+4.10); Windows ARM64 unmeasurable on its runner (CI90 -10.6..+18.2).
cpu_rule: WhyFS user-space CPU per stress iteration (collector + writer + service, the run and the 7 s after it, mean of 10) <= 1.5 x the frozen reference on the same hosted platform.  One calibration session per platform cannot separate changes below ~30-50 % from runner-to-runner variation (single iterations vary up to 1.39 x the mean); smaller changes are reported, not gated.
always_required: zero event loss (normal, discard and CPU sessions)
stress correctness: all 300 outputs labelled with their writer, complete, identity match
every event source enabled in the product configuration (the discard variant is diagnostic only)
always_reported: total overhead (the historical pre-1.0 rule: < 5 %) with CI90 and every raw pair
kernel/provider floor with CI90 and raw pairs
